recorded.prompt:q-sort-in-place: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-sort-in-place: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-sort-in-place: Page decides (a): "`List.add`, `remove` and `set` are each marked \"(optional operation)\" in the javadoc ... an implementation that doesn't support one throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. Throwing is part of `List`'s contract"; "`normalizeTags` is the code in breach: it relies on a promise `List` never made ... The fix builds a new list and leaves the argument alone". Run shows `stream().toList()  UnsupportedOperationException`. Minor gap: the page never says in-place sorting needs element writes (`set`); closest is the Reference row "`Arrays.asList` | `set` and `sort` work" and "every mutator throws" for `stream().toList()`.

recorded.pass:q-null-key: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-null-key: Page decides (c): "`Collection.contains` may throw `NullPointerException` \"if the specified element is null and this collection does not permit null elements (optional)\""; "`Set.of` rejects a null query the same way"; Reference row "`List.of(...).contains(null)`, `Set.of(...).contains(null)` | `NullPointerException` | kept: marked optional". Before-state shown by run row "Arrays.asList(...)  false", and "passes every test that sends the header and fails on the first request that doesn't". Note: Set.of is stated, not run; only List.of appears in the run.

recorded.prompt:q-shipping-rate: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-shipping-rate: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-shipping-rate: Page decides (c): heading "A Subtype May Accept More and Promise More, Never Less"; "A discount that also accepted a negative subtotal would break no caller, since none written against the interface sends one." Supported by statement only, no run. Wording risk: option c's reason is "checkout never sends a negative weight" (one caller's behaviour), whereas the page's reason is that no caller written against the interface sends one; d uses the same kind of caller-specific reason ("checkout rounds weights") and is wrong, so the distinguishing point rests on the interface contract, which c's text does not state.
